name: The Fruit -Conference Venue
narrative: Originally the Durham Fruit and Produce Company from 1926, this 22,000-square-foot warehouse once stored fruits arriving by train and now pulses as Durham's most experimental arts venue. Voted 'Best Kept Secret' and 'Best Place to Dance' in the Triangle, The Fruit bridges Durham's industrial tobacco-town roots with its vibrant creative present, hosting everything from EDM to photography showcases in a space that still features original loading dock doors and wooden beams.

name: The Durham Hotel -Welcome Party
narrative: Built in 1968 as the Home Savings and Loan headquarters, this mid-century modern landmark with its distinctive gold accents and angular tower has watched over downtown Durham's transformation for over 50 years. The only independently owned downtown hotel, it celebrates local character with Counter Culture coffee, Raleigh Denim blankets, and North Carolina artist installations, embodying Durham's past and present in Perry C. Langston's architectural icon.

name: 21c Museum Hotel Durham - Main
narrative: Housed in the 1930s Art Deco Durham Bank & Trust building designed by the same architects who created the Empire State Building, this contemporary art museum-hotel offers 10,500 square feet of free public exhibitions. Chef Melanie Wilkerson, a Durham native, leads Counting House restaurant celebrating North Carolina's coastal bounty, while the hotel serves as a cultural hub in the Research Triangle connecting international art with local culinary heritage.

name: 21c Museum Hotel Durham
narrative: This historic 1930s bank building transformed into a contemporary art museum and boutique hotel showcases rotating international exhibitions free to the public 24/7. Durham native Chef Melanie Wilkerson helms Counting House restaurant, serving Carolina's fresh seafood and local ingredients in a space where Art Deco details meet modern design, making it a destination for both art lovers and those seeking authentic North Carolina flavors.

name: The Durham Hotel
narrative: Perry C. Langston's 1968 mid-century masterpiece stands as downtown Durham's only independent hotel, with its iconic angled tower and gold facade symbolizing the city's architectural heritage. Inside, every detail celebrates North Carolina—Counter Culture coffee roasted locally, Raleigh Denim blankets, Burt's Bees amenities, and art by NC-based creators—creating a true Durham experience that honors both the building's history and the community's creative spirit.

name: Aloft Durham Downtown
narrative: This loft-inspired hotel sits adjacent to Durham Performing Arts Center in the American Tobacco Historic District, offering modern travelers prime access to the revitalized tobacco warehouses that once made Durham the tobacco capital of the world. With 134 rooms and WXYZ Lounge, it's perfectly positioned for experiencing downtown's transformation from industrial powerhouse to cultural destination.

name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Durham City View
narrative: Located in downtown Durham with skyline views, this 104-room hotel offers modern comfort within walking distance of Durham Central Park and the American Tobacco Campus. Its central location makes it an ideal base for exploring the Bull City's restaurants, breweries, and historic sites that tell the story of Durham's evolution from tobacco town to thriving innovation hub.

name: Unscripted Durham - JDV by Hyatt
narrative: Reimagined in 2017 and joining JdV by Hyatt in 2023, this 74-room boutique hotel in an iconic downtown building offers guests an authentic Durham experience with easy access to the American Tobacco Campus. Its location near Durham's entertainment district and thoughtful design make it a comfortable home base for exploring the city's vibrant food, arts, and brewery scene.

name: Durham Marriott City Center
narrative: Connected to the Durham Convention Center and steps from Carolina Theatre and Durham Performing Arts Center, this downtown hotel features Table South Kitchen & Bar serving Southern cuisine and local Starbucks coffee. With views of the Durham Bulls Athletic Park and within walking distance of American Tobacco Campus, it's positioned at the heart of the Bull City's revitalized downtown where visitors can experience Durham's transformation from tobacco powerhouse to cultural destination.

name: Aaktun Coffee, Restaurant and Bar
narrative: From the Mezcalito hospitality group and two-time James Beard semifinalist Chef Oscar Diaz, this Tulum-inspired spot transforms from daytime coffee cafe to upscale evening destination. With Mexican-influenced cuisine featuring fresh ingredients and tropical cenote-inspired decor, Aaktun showcases Durham's diverse culinary scene while bringing global flavors to downtown's Innovation District.

name: PRESS Coffee Crêpes Cocktails
narrative: This European-inspired cafe in American Tobacco Campus serves Durham-roasted Counter Culture Coffee alongside made-to-order crepes and craft cocktails in an Italian espresso bar meets Provencal bistro setting. With an open kitchen, separate cocktail bar, and covered patio overlooking the historic tobacco warehouses, PRESS offers 'A Carolina Twist' on European cafe culture using scratch-made dishes and local ingredients.

name: QueenBurger
narrative: Born from wildly popular pandemic pop-ups by Queeny's, this American Tobacco Campus smashburger spot grinds farm-raised, grass-fed North Carolina beef daily with house-made pickles, local cheese, and special sauce. Opening in 2020 and moving to brick-and-mortar, QueenBurger exemplifies Durham's innovative food scene with creative options like the PBJ burger with peanut butter and strawberry bacon jelly.

name: Bull City Burger and Brewery
narrative: Since 2011, Durham's longest-running brewpub has championed local agriculture with 100% pasture-raised, grass-fed NC beef ground in-house daily, house-made buns, condiments, and ingredients sourced from local farmers within 70 miles. This farm-to-fork establishment on East Parrish Street embodies Durham's commitment to sustainable, local food while supporting North Carolina's agricultural community.

name: Durham Food Hall
narrative: Durham's first food hall features 10 locally-owned vendors including Locals Seafood bringing NC coast-to-table offerings, Everything Bagels with avant-garde creations, and the Auctioneer Bar showcasing North Carolina spirits and beers. Housed at 530 Foster Street, this community gathering space emphasizes local sourcing and sustainability while celebrating Durham's diverse culinary talents and commitment to supporting neighborhood businesses.

name: Anjappar Chettinad Indian Restaurant, Durham
narrative: Part of the globally recognized Anjappar chain established in Chennai in 1964, this Downtown Durham location brings authentic South Indian Chettinad cuisine within walking distance of DPAC. With over 20 varieties of dosa and bold, aromatic dishes using fresh spices, it's quickly become a beloved addition to Durham's international food scene in the historic Register of Deeds building.

name: Mezcalito Durham
narrative: Opened in 2019 in Durham's food district, this vibrant Tex-Mex spot offers an extensive array of mezcal, tequila, and margaritas with fresh Mezcalito Mix in flavors from strawberry to passion fruit. With its festive atmosphere, family-friendly vibe, and walkable proximity to Ponysaurus Brewery, Mezcalito has become a Durham favorite for authentic Mexican flavors and creative cocktails.

name: Counting House
narrative: Led by Durham native Chef Melanie Wilkerson at 21c Museum Hotel, this restaurant celebrates North Carolina's rich seafood heritage in the historic Hill Building where the name references the space's banking past. The seafood-forward menu transforms regional coastal fare with playful execution and local ingredients, while the dining room features contemporary art, historic terrazzo floors, and double-height windows showcasing downtown Durham.

name: Thaiangle Restaurant
narrative: Opened in 2024 by the Ungsriwong family with over two decades in the restaurant business, this sophisticated Thai spot at 200 N. Mangum offers Chef's Special Crispy Duck, Salmon in Banana Leaves, and house-brewed Thai tea cocktails. Already voted Best Japanese Restaurant and Best New Restaurant by Indy Week readers, Thaiangle brings authentic Thai flavors with Durham flair to downtown's vibrant dining scene.

name: Queeny's
narrative: Open until 2 AM with a kitchen serving late-night comfort food, this uniquely Durham gathering place features arguably the best chicken tenders in town, killer burgers, and an on-site podcast studio plus Rubyfruit bookshop stocked with inclusive literature. Inspired by communal potluck spirit, Queeny's at 321 E. Chapel Hill Street hosts community events and brings casual, welcoming vibes to downtown's nightlife with options for vegetarians, vegans, and carnivores alike.

name: Gym Tacos
narrative: Since 2019, Gym Tacos has brought authentic Mexican flavor to Durham's center with handmade corn tortillas, traditional tacos, tortas, and tostadas that locals rave are 'the best tacos I ever had.' Located at 102 City Hall Plaza with bright, casual atmosphere perfect for family gatherings or happy hour, this is the taqueria Durham needed to satisfy cravings for genuine Mexican street food.

name: Luna Rotisserie and Empanadas
narrative: Established in 2015 at 112 W Main Street, this casual fusion spot serves South American-inspired empanadas, arepas, and Luna Grain Bowls with generous portions of perfectly seasoned chicken, pork, and brisket. As one of the top restaurants near DPAC, Luna brings flavorful Latin American comfort food to downtown Durham's thriving culinary landscape.

name: Dashi Ramen and Izakaya Cocktail Bar
narrative: This two-story Japanese restaurant opened in February to immediate acclaim, voted Best Japanese Restaurant and Best New Restaurant by Indy Week readers. The first-floor ramen shop serves steamy bowls in a cozy open kitchen, while the upstairs izakaya features an 18-page drink menu (a mecca for whiskey enthusiasts) and omakase dining, with both vegan and gluten-free options available in downtown Durham.

name: Barsa New Indian
narrative: Under new management with a chef from Michelin-starred restaurants who grinds and blends fresh herbs and spices daily, Barsa was voted 'The Best Indian Restaurant in the Triangle' by The News & Observer. Led by chef Vinod Kumar (formerly of NYC's Michelin-starred Semma), this modern upscale spot at 105 W Morgan Street reimagines beloved Indian flavors with dishes like Lobster Moilee and banana leaf-wrapped salmon.

name: Pokeworks
narrative: This build-your-own poke restaurant at 122 W Main Street emphasizes fresh, healthy Hawaiian-inspired bowls, burritos, and salads with responsibly-sourced seafood. With customizable options for vegans and gluten-free diners, plus signature works featuring ahi tuna, salmon, free-range chicken, and tofu, Pokeworks brings island flavors and nutritious fast-casual dining to downtown Durham.

name: Pizzeria Toro
narrative: Since opening at 105 E Chapel Hill Street, this wood-fired pizzeria has earned acclaim for authentic Italian-style pizza that an Italian friend called 'the best outside of his country.' Using North Carolina ingredients like local corn, okra, and tomatoes with pizza perfectly baked in their central wood-burning oven, Pizzeria Toro has become a beloved Durham destination where the kale salad ranks among the city's most popular dishes.

name: Pie Pushers
narrative: Starting as a food truck and evolving to a downtown location plus concessions at Durham Bulls Athletic Park, Pie Pushers serves 'Durham-style' hand-tossed thin crust pizza using a decade-perfected family recipe. With their motto 'Local Pies for the People,' they top pizzas with seasonal, eclectic ingredients supporting local farmers and artisans, offering gluten-free and vegan options that showcase Durham's creative food scene.

name: koki - Creative Puerto Rican Kitchen
narrative: Originally launched as food truck Spanglish in 2016, koki now serves modern Puerto Rican cuisine at 104 City Hall Plaza with breakfast, lunch, and dinner including empanadas, mofongo, rice bowls, and sandwiches. Their motto 'Barriga Llena, Corazón Contento' (Full Belly, Happy Heart) captures the warm spirit of this locally-owned spot bringing authentic Puerto Rican flavors with keto, vegan, and vegetarian options to downtown Durham.

name: Parker and Otis
narrative: Created by Jennings Brody at American Tobacco Campus, this quaint European-style cafe serves Counter Culture Coffee roasted in Durham, legendary iced coffee, fresh breakfast and lunch with local ingredients, plus a gourmet market featuring NC products, specialty foods, cheese, wine, and gifts. The Avocado Toast, Pimento Cheese sandwich, and spectacular cheddar biscuits showcase Durham's commitment to quality local ingredients in a charming setting.

name: Viceroy
narrative: This British pub meets Indian restaurant at 335 W Main Street serves Classic Indian and fusion fare like curried shepherd's pie in an atmosphere reminiscent of London with vintage decor and historic Indian portraits. Open since 2015, Viceroy has earned a 4.6 rating on OpenTable with customers calling it '#1 of the best restaurant in downtown Durham' for its top-shelf service, unique flavors, and extensive menu including several vegan options.

name: Seraphine
narrative: From local restaurateurs Graham and Brad Weddington, Seraphine brings Louisiana-inspired cuisine to American Tobacco Campus with raw oysters, barbeque shrimp, fried catfish, shrimp and grits, and beignets. This New Orleans-style spot explores family Louisiana heritage through modern interpretations of Southern classics, offering warmth, carefully crafted cocktails, and attractive outdoor patio dining in the heart of downtown Durham.

name: Mateo Bar de Tapas
narrative: Since 2012, chef Matthew Kelly's first solo venture has blended Spanish heart with Southern soul in the old Book Exchange building at 109 W Chapel Hill Street. Offering Spanish small plates with Southern inflection and one of the largest sherry collections in the country, Mateo serves dishes like Pan Con Tomate that customers call 'the best I've ever had, including in Spain,' making it a perfect pre-DPAC dining destination.

name: Alley Twenty Six
narrative: Opened in 2012 by Shannon Healy as North Carolina's first James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Bar Program, this craft cocktail pioneer at 320 E Chapel Hill Street crafts seasonally-based drinks with locally sourced ingredients. With Chef Carrie Schleiffer's upscale food pairings added in 2017, plus house-made syrups and tonic, Alley Twenty Six continues to set Durham's standard for artisanal cocktails and creative bartending.

name: M Sushi
narrative: Chef Mike Lee's flagship restaurant was the Triangle's first dedicated sushi and seafood restaurant, now with two locations including downtown Durham's minimalist vault-like den. Part of the acclaimed M Restaurants group (including M Tempura named one of Bon Appetit's top 50 best new restaurants in 2019), M Sushi showcases high-quality ingredients and expert Japanese craftsmanship in the heart of Bull City.

name: Little Bull
narrative: Chef Oscar Diaz, who refined his skills at Michelin-starred Alizé in Las Vegas, opened Little Bull at 810 N Mangum to showcase 'Pocho cuisine'—sincere comfort food inspired by first-generation immigrant kids. The menu features innovative Mexican-American fusion like birria dumplings with goat, whole NC speckled trout, and grilled octopus, earning regional acclaim as one of the Triangle's top restaurants celebrating immigrant influence on American food.

name: Bar Virgile
narrative: Since 2006, Bar Virgile at 105 S Mangum has been serving craft and classic cocktails with an ever-changing dinner and small plates menu near Durham Performing Arts Center and Carolina Theater. With talented bartenders spinning fresh-ingredient cocktails at reasonable prices in a space featuring a wonderful stamped metal ceiling and New Orleans ambience, this downtown gem offers one of the top 10 burgers in the area and no-reservation walk-in service.

name: Rue Cler
narrative: Since 2006, Rue Cler has brought simple, classic French preparations to downtown Durham at 401 E Chapel Hill Street, inspired by Parisian neighborhood restaurants. Chef Todd Whitney's kitchen uses southeastern ingredients and seasonal, local products including baguettes from Durham's Loaf bakery, serving beloved dishes like coq au vin, duck confit, and steak frites with warm, friendly service that greets regulars by name.

name: NanaSteak
narrative: Opened in February 2016 next to Durham Performing Arts Center and Aloft Hotel, NanaSteak pays homage to Durham's tobacco history with bar tops and tables inlaid with real tobacco leaves crafted by Artisan Leaf. This upscale steakhouse offers North Carolina fare and an award-winning Wine Spectator wine program, celebrating Durham's past while serving contemporary diners in the revitalized American Tobacco Campus.

name: M Tempura
narrative: Named by Bon Appetit as one of the top 50 best new restaurants in the country in 2019, M Tempura at 311 Holland Street is one of only a handful of true tempura restaurants on the East Coast. Part of Chef Mike Lee's M Restaurants group and home to Chef Savannah Miller (Top Chef season 21), it showcases expert Japanese tempura craftsmanship alongside Durham's innovative culinary scene.

name: Nerra
narrative: Led by Durham native Executive Chef Lex at 506 Ramseur Street, this seasonal, seafood-forward restaurant partners with local NC farmers, fishers, and foragers to create a menu celebrating the Carolinas' coastal traditions. From briny shellfish and coastal catches to charred vegetables and heirloom grains, Nerra blends local sourcing with global technique in a rustic nautical space featuring a marble bar and cozy patio.

name: Flying Bull Restaurant and Brewery
narrative: Starting in Durham's 9th Street neighborhood in 2020 and expanding to Morris Street in 2024, this veteran-owned and women-owned brewery showcases 20 innovative Durham-crafted beers from Old World classics to New England IPAs. Rooted in building community through good food and great beer, Flying Bull has been voted one of Durham's Best Breweries while supporting local causes and collaborating with neighborhood makers.

name: M Pocha
narrative: Part of Chef Mike Lee's acclaimed M Restaurants group, M Pocha serves Korean street food inspired by Pojanmacha ('Tented Cart on Wheels') in a brick-and-mortar style similar to Japanese izakaya. With tapas-style dishes meant for sharing while drinking, M Pocha brings authentic Korean pub culture to Durham's diverse international dining scene alongside sister restaurants M Sushi and M Tempura.

name: Mothers & Sons Trattoria
narrative: Chef Matthew Kelly and Josh 'Skinny' DeCarolis opened this regional Italian trattoria at 107 W. Chapel Hill Street in 2016, featuring handmade pasta fatta a mano—the first restaurant in the South focused on this craft. With seasonal dishes like bucatini al amatriciana and squid ink tonnarelli, plus wood-fired fare, Mothers & Sons showcases Kelly's expertise from his work at Fearrington House, Vin Rouge, and Mateo.

name: Cucciolo Osteria Durham
narrative: Cousins Jimmy and Julian Kim brought their modern Italian concept from Seoul to Durham's West Main Street in 2018, offering pasta specialties from classic Cacio e Pepe to Truffle Tajarin and unique bruschette. With an intimate, cozy space always busy with Durham diners enjoying impeccable service and dishes like butter chicken and Porchetta, Cucciolo has become a top-rated destination requiring advance reservations.

name: delafia
narrative: This wine bar and retail shop at 1103 S Roxboro Street specializes in natural wines—the farm-to-table version of wine made on smaller scale with minimal intervention. With a rapidly changing by-the-glass list, extensive retail selection, large patio, and funky wines from small producers, delafia offers gritty speakeasy vibes in a somewhat hidden corner white brick building, serving Durham's natural wine lovers with rotating selections and intimate atmosphere.

name: Weldon Mills Distillery Durham
narrative: The most awarded small batch spirits distillery and #1 Micro-Distillery in America opened its second location downtown at 300 E. Main Street in March 2023. This speakeasy-like space produces bourbon, whiskey, vodka, gin, rum, and tequila using NC corn, malted wheat, barley, and Roanoke River water, earning top honors including Best Distillery 2022-2023 and serving as Official Spirit of the Durham Bulls.

name: Honeygirl Meadery & Tasting Room
narrative: At American Tobacco Campus (312 Blackwell Street), Durham's award-winning urban meadery celebrates honeybees by fermenting local and global true source honey with NC fruits, flowers, and herbs into small-batch seasonal meads. Now part of Ment Beverage Co., Honeygirl offers flights, tastings, and bottles in an open, beautiful space while supporting Bee Downtown and Bee City Durham initiatives for pollinators.

name: Bull City Ciderworks Durham
narrative: Founded in a backyard cutting North Carolina apples with a modified garbage disposal grinder, Bull City Ciderworks now operates three taprooms including the Durham location at 305 S Roxboro Street. Making ciders with 100% apple juice never back-sweetened with corn syrup, they bridge wine and beer using unique local ingredients like hops, tea, honey, and ginger—producing roughly 5,500 gallons per batch of over 70 award-winning ciders.

name: Ponysaurus Brewing Co.
narrative: Starting in an attic above The Cookery in 2015, Ponysaurus has become one of Durham's most inventive breweries at 219 Hood Street with one of the largest outdoor patios in the city. Named a 'Next Level Brewery' by Food & Wine and brewing 'the best pint in Durham' per Thrillist, this Durham-native brewery creates beer for everyone to enjoy with fire pits, wood benches, and string lights in the Downtown East neighborhood.

name: Fullsteam
narrative: Since 2010, Fullsteam has pioneered the Southern Beer Economy, purchasing over $850,000 in Southern-farmed ingredients from local barley to foraged black walnuts. As a Craft Malt Certified brewery, their Plow to Pint beers use 100% North Carolina malt, seasonal fruits like persimmons and paw paws, sweet potatoes, and basil—building a landmark location at Durham's American Tobacco Campus while maintaining their Boxyard RTP taproom.

name: The Velvet Hippo Bar & Lounge
narrative: Opening August 2023 on the third-floor rooftop at 119 Orange Street, this tropical neighborhood bar for everybody offers signature cocktails, local beers, creative mocktails, and light bites from Chef Regina Jones. Named as a nickname for the owner's pitbull pup, The Velvet Hippo creates vacation vibes in downtown Durham with dog-friendly 'Yappy Hours' on weekends and Latin nights every 1st and 3rd Friday.

name: Dram and Draught
narrative: Since 2016, this private club (21+ only) at 701 W. Main Street has served Durham's whiskey fanatics, craft beer fans, cocktail enthusiasts, and wine lovers as a great neighborhood bar. With over 300 whiskeys from around the world, hand-crafted cocktails, draught beer from Raleigh and beyond, and super friendly, knowledgeable staff, Dram & Draught offers a chilled, laid-back environment for slow sipping and exploring new spirits.

name: Boxcar Bar + Arcade
narrative: Located at 621 Foster Street overlooking historic Durham Athletic Park, Boxcar features 70+ classic and modern arcade games including Pac-Man, Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat, NBA Jam, plus skeeball, air hockey, and DDR. With a 7,000 square foot patio with fire pits, outdoor games, live music, local beers, seasonal cocktails, and fresh pizzas, this entertainment venue hosts Tuesday karaoke and Wednesday skeeball tournaments in downtown Durham.

name: Kingfisher
narrative: Opening in 2019 as one of the country's best new cocktail bars and North Carolina's second James Beard Awards Outstanding Bar Program semifinalist, Kingfisher at 321 E. Chapel Hill Street crafts ground-to-glass cocktails in handmade ceramic glassware. This intimate underground speakeasy beside The Durham Hotel highlights NC produce, foraged ingredients, and local products—like preserved strawberries from Lil' Farm in Timberlake—with regular jazz nights and a backyard garden.

name: Hi-Wire Brewing Durham
narrative: Asheville's Hi-Wire Brewing opened their first taproom outside Asheville at Golden Belt (800 Taylor Street) in 2018, featuring 8,844 square feet with an outdoor covered patio and beer garden. With 24 taps pouring Hi-Wire's full lineup including Hi-Wire Lager, Bed of Nails Brown, and Hi-Pitch Mosaic IPA, plus shuffleboard, soccer pool, table tennis, and Neapolitan pizza from neighboring Cugino Forno, it's a game-heavy destination for craft beer enthusiasts.

name: West End Social
narrative: Durham's Original Wine Bar since 1997 at 601 W Main Street offers over 40 wines by the glass, custom cocktails, two dozen beers, and upscale food from Chef Carrie Schleiffer in a lounge with upstairs mezzanine and outdoor patio. With local cheese plates, specialty entrees, and extensive board game selection, West End Social provides elegant atmosphere perfect for casual nights or dressed-up date nights between downtown and Brightleaf District.

name: DSSOLVR Durham
narrative: This Asheville-based brewery's 2023 Durham taproom at 630 Rigsbee Avenue serves 20 drafts ranging from Mexican lagers to hazy IPAs, including their best-selling Cold Caprese Pizza Italian Pilsner. With psychedelic alien-themed art, dog-friendly atmosphere, free NES gameplay, weekly art workshops, and partnerships with local restaurants, DSSOLVR brings surreal, experimental brewing—brewed till surreal—plus hard seltzers, gluten-free sours, natural wine, and ciders to the Warehouse District.

name: Congress Social Bar
narrative: East Durham's neighborhood joy bar, music spot, and event space at 471 South Driver Street creates a third place for the community—a Black-owned convivial gathering spot where neighbors linger and connect. With amazing BBQ from Mike Ds next door, Hip Hop, R&B, and Soca from DJs, and food trucks like Amagees Jamaican outside, Congress offers grown and sexy vibes in an upcoming section where Black-owned businesses are transforming East Durham.

name: La Mala Mexican Inspired Cocktails
narrative: This trendy downtown spot at 110 Corcoran Street brings Mexican-inspired cocktails made with freshly squeezed fruits and high-quality tequilas, plus authentic street food made fresh daily. With Latin music from DJs on Friday nights, drinks like the glow-in-the-dark La Buenota, beautiful murals for photos, and a location perfect for pre-DPAC shows, La Mala offers vibrant dining and bar-hopping energy to downtown Durham.

name: Fizzwerks
narrative: Durham's first seltzer brewery opened March 2024 at 618 Ramseur Street, brewing hard seltzers with fresh fruits (peach from orchards two hours south, cantaloupe from owners' garden), botanicals, and teas. Inside a former tile factory with the best roof deck in Durham seating 200, Fizzwerks also serves hard root beer, Delta-9 drinks, nonalcoholic seltzers, and fresh shareable foods like flatbreads, sandwiches, and homemade pierogies using seasonal local ingredients.

name: Durham Beer Garden
narrative: Located on North Mangum Street in Old Five Points, this family- and dog-friendly space features 20 rotating taps including Durham's Durty Bull Extra Crispy Pilsner and Booneshine High Country Honey. With 18 TVs, expansive indoor/outdoor areas for large groups, and Music on Mangum events every Saturday night 6-9 PM, Durham Beer Garden provides a refreshing casual atmosphere dedicated to beer, food, and camaraderie.

name: High Dive Durham
narrative: Opening August 2024 at 101 W Main Street from the owners of Bar Virgile and Annexe, High Dive offers stylish dive bar charm with pool, darts, foosball, pinball, Golden Tee, vintage jukebox, and some of Durham's cheapest drinks. This hidden gem in the old Quarter Horse location provides classy dive bar vibes without pretentiousness, featuring house-made pickled jalapeños, customized foosball table, free popcorn, and non-alcoholic options.

name: The Daily Beer Bar
narrative: Opened December 2022 by former Hop Culture Managing Editor John Paradiso at 108 E Main Street, The Daily serves Yonder Coffee and local bakery pastries in morning, sandwiches with local ingredients for lunch, and 30+ rotating local artisanal beers into evening. This independently-owned neighborhood bar and cafe creates a cozy, relaxed atmosphere perfect for catching up with friends or quiet time with a book—quickly becoming one of Durham's best hidden-gem drinking spots.

name: Baryo
narrative: At Durham Bottling Co. (506 Ramseur Street), Baryo serves morning espresso, afternoon wine, late-night cocktails, and zero-proof THC creations in Durham's gathering place for every moment. This coffee and cocktail bar inspired by Durham's resilience and reinvention fosters conversation and community with beautiful patio, calming vibes, great wifi for remote work, and food available next door from Krill restaurant in the historic bottling company space.

name: The Glass Jug Beer Lab - Downtown Durham
narrative: This family-run brewery next to Durham Central Park at 800 Taylor Street produces small-batch experimental beers including award-winning craft beer and gluten-free hard ginger beer. With their Beer Lab's scientific brewing approach, 10 rotating draft taps, unique batch-made cocktails featuring NC spirits, weekly run/cycling clubs, disc golf league, live music, trivia, and vinyl record nights, they create warm, inviting atmosphere for beer lovers and beyond.

name: Rhythm & Brews Bar and Grill
narrative: Durham's hottest spot for great drinks, delicious food, and unforgettable nights opened September 2024 at 908 Fayetteville Street, blending mouthwatering food from classic bar fare to innovative signature dishes with creative cocktails in a lively, music-inspired atmosphere. This Black-owned establishment offers signature cocktails, mocktails, local brews, and international favorites with friendly staff creating inviting ambiance for casual nights or special celebrations.

name: Durty Bull Brewing Company
narrative: Chosen by Beer Advocate as one of the Class of 2016's 34 Best New Breweries in the US, Durty Bull at 206 Broadway Street specializes in IPAs, lagers, and award-winning seltzers in a 6,000 square foot, 15-barrel production brewery. Half a mile from City Center near Central Park, this downtown taproom employs modern approaches on classic styles with comedy in the barrel room, live patio shows, and strong Durham community involvement.

name: Atomic Clock Brewing Company
narrative: Brother-sister duo Brian and Colleen Quinn opened Atomic Clock in early 2024 at 501 Washington Street in Durham's historic fleet maintenance garage, representing their brewing philosophy—continuous pursuit of perfection through precision. With a 20-barrel brewhouse at 606 United Drive, this downtown taproom serves IPAs, lagers, barrel aged and sour beers, plus full-service kitchen, cocktails, and wine in a 6,000 square foot space with charming, modern approach to classic styles.

name: Ramblers Beer & Wine
narrative: This cozy neighborhood spot at 701 W Main Street serves craft beer, natural wine, and simple shareable snacks in a relaxed atmosphere perfect for conversation. With rotating taps featuring local and regional breweries, thoughtfully curated wine selections, and a welcoming vibe, Ramblers has become a beloved Durham gathering place for beer and wine enthusiasts seeking quality drinks without pretension.

name: Clouds Brewing - Durham Brewcade + Kitchen
narrative: Opening October 2016 in Brightleaf Square, Clouds features 50 taps (30 house brews, 20 guests) including a 10-tap self-pour beer wall with RFID wristband sampling. This German-inspired brewpub with rustic warehouse vibe offers burgers, beer-brined brats, wings, tacos, vegan options, weekend brunch, plus pool tables, arcade games, TVs for Duke games, dog-friendly patio, and space for up to 150 guests—perfect for Durham's casual entertainment.

name: The Waiting Room
narrative: Tucked in the American Tobacco building basement at 300 Blackwell Street, this chic speakeasy lounge from the Nomad team opened as Durham's waiting room before DPAC shows. With innovative cocktails like the Old Bull featuring Durham Distillery's Conniption Gin, small plates, Raleigh Bakehouse desserts, cozy couches and window seats, The Waiting Room creates inclusive space for perfectly crafted drinks in an intimate, relaxing 21+ private club atmosphere.

name: Bull Durham Beer Company
narrative: The only craft brewery in Minor League Baseball owned by a team, Bull Durham Beer Company operates inside Durham Bulls Athletic Park at 409 Blackwell Street and American Tobacco Campus. Led by Executive Brewmaster Sebastian Wolfrum, BDBCo brings fresh, local beer to Bulls fans at the ballpark, celebrating Durham's connection to baseball heritage, the iconic 'Bull Durham' film, and the city's craft brewing innovation.

name: Bull City Burger and Brewery
narrative: Since 2011, Durham's longest-running brewpub has championed local agriculture with 100% pasture-raised, grass-fed NC beef ground in-house daily, house-made buns, condiments, and ingredients sourced from local farmers within 70 miles. This farm-to-fork establishment on East Parrish Street embodies Durham's commitment to sustainable, local food while supporting North Carolina's agricultural community.

name: Killer Queen Wine Bar
narrative: Located at 117 E Main Street with hours Tuesday-Saturday, Killer Queen offers fantastic rotating selection of white, red, rose, orange, and sparkling wines with a focus on natural wines. This cute, cozy spot feels like walking into your best friend's living room with counter seating, small food menu with charcuterie and warm chocolate chip cookies, cozy patio with blankets and heat lamps, and free wine tastings every Wednesday 6-8pm.

name: Coupe & Stein Champagne Bar
narrative: Durham's newest destination for refined relaxation opened at 800 Taylor Street in the historic warehouse district, featuring champagne, crafted cocktails, and exclusive selections in a beautifully curated space with a charming pink piano. With elegant decor, warm lighting, and welcoming atmosphere, Coupe & Stein creates perfect environment for intimate conversations and memorable celebrations in Durham's growing craft beverage scene.

name: Primrose Bar and Lounge
narrative: Opening in 2024 at 111 W Main Street, this whimsical lounge adorned with floral wallpaper and rose-covered facades serves innovative cocktails with playful, internet-inflected sensibilities like 'Becky with the Good Pear' and 'Sippin' on Some Sizzurp.' With movie nights Monday-Tuesday, live music, signature drinks, comfy seating, and location perfect for post-DPAC cocktails, Primrose brings great energy and unique botanical-inspired ambiance to downtown Durham.

name: West End Social
narrative: Durham's Original Wine Bar since 1997 at 601 W Main Street offers over 40 wines by the glass, custom cocktails, two dozen beers, and upscale food from Chef Carrie Schleiffer in a lounge with upstairs mezzanine and outdoor patio. With local cheese plates, specialty entrees, and extensive board game selection, West End Social provides elegant atmosphere perfect for casual nights or dressed-up date nights between downtown and Brightleaf District.

name: Conniption Bar & Lounge - Formerly known as Corpse Reviver Bar & Lounge
Pour Taproom
narrative: Starting in Asheville in 2014 and expanding to downtown Durham at 202 Corcoran Street opposite the Bull at CCB Plaza, Pour Taproom offers 60+ self-serve taps where guests pour their own beer, cider, wine, and kombucha by the ounce using smart wristbands. With in-house catering from Lula & Sadie's, board games, cornhole, large patio overlooking Bull City, and space for 10-100 guests, Pour showcases local craft beverages with innovative self-serve technology.

name: American Tobacco Campus
narrative: Once headquarters of American Tobacco Company controlling 90% of the U.S. tobacco market, these 1874-1950s warehouses sat vacant after 1987 closure until Capitol Broadcasting Company's $200 million 2001 transformation. Now a million-square-foot campus with iconic Lucky Strike smokestack, Bull River water feature, creative offices (GlaxoSmithKline, Duke, Burt's Bees, American Underground tech hub), restaurants, and DPAC—drawing one million+ visitors yearly to this nationally recognized historic reuse success story.

name: Durham Bulls Athletic Park
narrative: Opening in 1995, this 10,000-seat ballpark designed by HOK Sport features the 32-foot Blue Monster wall and manual scoreboard reminiscent of Fenway's Green Monster. Home to Triple-A Durham Bulls (Tampa Bay Rays affiliate) who jumped from Class A to Triple-A in 1998 partly due to 'Bull Durham' film fame, the park has hosted three Triple-A National Championships (2009, 2017, 2022) and houses Bull Durham Beer Company—the only brewery owned by a Minor League team.

name: Museum of Durham History
narrative: The Duke Homestead State Historic Site and Tobacco Museum preserves 5,500 square feet of exhibits on tobacco farming, manufacturing, and advertising at Washington Duke's 1852 home and 1869 tobacco factory. This National Historic Landmark tells how Duke's vision after the Civil War transformed North Carolina into the heart of a worldwide tobacco empire, with Duke family money founding today's Duke University, hospitals, and facilities that improved millions of Southerners' lives.

name: Durham Central Park
narrative: Located at 501 Foster Street, this downtown park hosts the Durham Farmers' Market—established 1998 and operating year-round since 2007 under the Pavilion. With 50+ vendors from within 70 miles selling produce they grew themselves, Double Bucks for SNAP clients, Senior Farmers Market program, plus Durham Craft Market and Art Market Durham happening simultaneously on weekends, the park embodies Durham's eclectic community vibe with music, skateboarders, and that great Durham energy.

name: Boxcar Bar + Arcade
narrative: Located at 621 Foster Street overlooking historic Durham Athletic Park, Boxcar features 70+ classic and modern arcade games including Pac-Man, Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat, NBA Jam, plus skeeball, air hockey, and DDR. With a 7,000 square foot patio with fire pits, outdoor games, live music, local beers, seasonal cocktails, and fresh pizzas, this entertainment venue hosts Tuesday karaoke and Wednesday skeeball tournaments in downtown Durham.

name: Aaktun Coffee, Restaurant and Bar
narrative: From the Mezcalito hospitality group and two-time James Beard semifinalist Chef Oscar Diaz, this Tulum-inspired spot transforms from daytime coffee cafe to upscale evening destination. With Mexican-influenced cuisine featuring fresh ingredients and tropical cenote-inspired decor, Aaktun showcases Durham's diverse culinary scene while bringing global flavors to downtown's Innovation District.

name: Yonder Coffee
narrative: Located at 108 E Main Street inside The Daily Beer Bar, Yonder Coffee is a true specialty coffee destination keeping varieties from many different global roasters on rotation. Offering coffee flights from 3 roasters with origin cards, a Global Roaster Subscription featuring 12 countries over 12 months, unique drinks like Espresso Tonic and Tiramisu Iced Coffee, plus eclectic atmosphere with spinning vinyl, Yonder provides exceptional specialty coffee experiences throughout the day.

name: Cocoa Cinnamon
narrative: Founded by Areli Barrera Grodski and Leon Grodski Barrera in 2010 and growing in Durham since 2011, Cocoa Cinnamon operates three cafes with their Little Waves Coffee Roasters (opened 2017) earning international recognition. This Latina co-owned, women-forward business with team representing 10+ countries and 8 languages has been featured in Food Network's '51 Best Coffee Shops in America,' blending cultural heritage, sustainability, and local pride as a beloved Durham community hub.

name: The Oak House Durham
narrative: Opening in 2019 on the ground floor of One City Center at 126 W Main Street, The Oak House serves Caballo Rojo coffee roasted on-site, craft beer, cider, fine wine, and hosts coffee roasting demonstrations, cuppings, tastings, and live music. With ample seating, outlets, and late-night hours, this craft coffee/wine bar concept welcomes everyone in Durham's thriving community as a cozy study spot and evening social gathering space.

name: PRESS Coffee Crêpes Cocktails
narrative: This European-inspired cafe in American Tobacco Campus serves Durham-roasted Counter Culture Coffee alongside made-to-order crepes and craft cocktails in an Italian espresso bar meets Provencal bistro setting. With an open kitchen, separate cocktail bar, and covered patio overlooking the historic tobacco warehouses, PRESS offers 'A Carolina Twist' on European cafe culture using scratch-made dishes and local ingredients.

name: Narrative Coffee Company
narrative: Born in Raleigh from a belief that coffee brings people together and creates shared stories, Narrative opened their first brick-and-mortar at 300 Morris Street in Durham Innovation District after building following throughout Triangle with their trailer and cart. Serving high quality specialty coffee, free wifi, and welcoming workspace at markets, festivals, and neighborhood gatherings, Narrative fosters connections and community through daily coffee rituals that create happiness and meaningful interactions.

name: Foster Street Coffee
narrative: Opened by Tracy Cooper (20+ years in corporate finance) at 530 Foster Street in Liberty Warehouse Building north of Central Park, this hometown coffee shop works with Valerio Coffee Roasters and local roasters serving eight-bean espresso blend. With pastries from Durham's Crumbs Bakery, Scratch Bakery, Ninth Street Bakery, Strong Arm Baking, and Micheal's English Muffins, plus MajaTei teas and organic smoothies, Foster Street brings global inspiration and local produce to downtown Durham.

name: Yonderlust Cafe
narrative: This local family-owned cafe and outdoor gear shop at 109 N. Gregson Street in downtown Durham serves Joe Van Gogh Coffee roasted in Durham. As a neighborhood gathering spot combining coffee service with outdoor adventure supplies, Yonderlust embodies Durham's community spirit while serving quality locally-roasted coffee to residents and visitors exploring the Bull City.

name: Nectar Cafe
narrative: Located at 620 Foster Street in the Geerhouse lobby, this bright modern cafe offers Counter Culture Coffee, matcha lattes, lemonades, wine, beer, and pastries from Raleigh's Lucettegrace in a cathedral-like space with floor-to-ceiling windows. From the owners of Foster Street Coffee, Nectar transitions seamlessly from morning pastries to lunch destination with traditional fare plus vegan and gluten-free options, featuring a dog-friendly mint-green bistro patio perfect for remote workers.
